why: metrics.json stores the best-epoch validation value under one name and the pipeline recomputes the same quantity under another: two names, one number, not a second opinion on the model.
early stopping fires at best_ep + patience, so by definition no improvement exists inside a converged run's final patience window; informative only for budget_limited cells.
the baseline compared with itself: numerator and denominator are the same six numbers. It tests the arithmetic, not a module.

arms with different parameter counts must report different counts; one value for every arm means the field is a constant. Precedent: arm_build_ok.py printed params=119364 for B0/B1/B2/B3 while metrics.json reports 115010/119364/115139/115139 -- and 119364 is B1's true count, which is what makes the wrong number believable.

when both ensembles already have the same number of members, the equal-size control rebuilds the baseline from exactly the same seeds, so it is the same average and must return the same number. A gap here would mean the control changed something other than the member count.

a normal critical value in place of t(df) does not change the point estimate, it only narrows the interval -- and it narrows it exactly where the engine counts are large, which is where the closest calls live. Recomputing half/se and comparing with t(df) is the only check that can see a wrong critical value, because every other column is unchanged by it.
